subject.title: fix: block WhatsApp direct sends during reachout timelock

question: Should WhatsApp direct sends fail early when Baileys reports an active reachout timelock, or should this PR stay diagnostic-only while the broader outbound diagnostics work remains open?
rationale: The code path is now plausible, but the change deliberately turns a late transport failure into an early OpenClaw failure for existing direct-send workflows.

options.title: Accept the plugin guard after green checks
options.body: Keep the guard in the WhatsApp plugin, require green exact-head or merge-ref validation, and merge once channel owners are satisfied with the fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Defer fail-closed behavior
options.body: Leave this PR open or narrow it while the broader diagnostics PR decides trusted-contact and timelock handling together.

options.title: Keep late transport behavior
options.body: Close or retarget this PR if maintainers want WhatsApp/Baileys to remain the only authority that rejects these sends at runtime.

recommendation.title: Accept the plugin guard after green checks
recommendation.body: Keep the guard in the WhatsApp plugin, require green exact-head or merge-ref validation, and merge once channel owners are satisfied with the fail-closed behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored this PR and have the strongest recent merged history across the affected WhatsApp send and QA paths.
